summary.declined_reason: All three target backend/.env which was never committed to version control (excluded by .gitignore); CONFIRMED=false at this revision

patches.title: Password reset token has no dedicated type claim — type confusion allows access tokens to reset passwords
get_current_user accepts any JWT regardless of purpose claim
OAuth state parameter has no HMAC — forged state enables token injection into arbitrary user accounts
patches.note: Addresses the same root vulnerability as F11. Apply one or the other — not both.

patches.title: Password reset token can be replayed after first use — no JTI blocklist
JWT tokens stored in localStorage — readable by any same-origin script (XSS)
patches.note: Addresses the same root vulnerability as F19. Apply one or the other — not both.

patches.title: require_approval IDOR — approval gate does not verify requested_by matches current user
gmail_send fetches Message by UUID with no ownership check (IDOR)
OAuth state parameter contains no random nonce — token injection into arbitrary user accounts
patches.note: Addresses the same root vulnerability as F5. Apply one or the other — not both.

patches.title: IDOR: resolve_validation lookup not scoped to the route's listing_id
list_documents exposes all documents to any authenticated user — no ownership filter
get_document fetches any document by caller-supplied UUID with no ownership check (IDOR)
update_user allows a manage_users holder to escalate their own role to any higher-privilege role
patches.note: Closes the self-escalation path only. Cross-user privilege assignment (manage_users holder promoting another account to admin) is a separate pre-existing gap tracked outside this patch set.

patches.title: COPY . . bakes .env secrets into Docker image layer — no .dockerignore present
Hardcoded trivially-weak Postgres credentials committed to version control
Refresh Token Never Revoked on Logout — Server-Side Session Remains Active
JWT access and refresh tokens persisted in localStorage, exposed to any same-origin script
patches.note: Addresses the same root vulnerability as F8. Apply one or the other — not both.
